parsed.doc_summary: LAHD page on the LA Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO): covers non-RSO units, at-fault and no-fault grounds, relocation assistance, non-payment threshold (FMR), and filing of eviction notices. It also mentions state AB 1482 rent limits, but only as context.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords of covered LA units may end a tenancy only for listed at-fault reasons or no-fault reasons. No-fault evictions require relocation assistance. Evictions for unpaid rent are barred unless the amount owed exceeds Fair Market Rent for the unit size. All eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.effective_date_note: The page gives no effective date for the core JCO. Related items: non-payment FMR threshold effective 2023-03-27, and Notice of Right to Counsel posting from 2025-08-20.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless or substance-abuse treatment facilities, some HACLA or government properties. Units covered by the RSO are governed by the RSO instead. Tenant must have lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease must have expired.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in LA not regulated by the RSO. Can apply to buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and to single-family dwellings.
rules.interaction: Applies to units not covered by the RSO. The page says the JCO does not regulate rent increases. State AB 1482 may still apply to rent increases.
rules.conflict_note: The page does not cite a municipal code section. The code citation is not stated in the document.

no_rule_findings.finding: The JCO itself does not regulate rent increases. Units outside the RSO fall under the state AB 1482 cap, not a JCO cap.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The JCO does not regulate rent increases, however, state law
